variants: Go2 AIR, PRO, X and EDU on the product page. Full secondary development is an EDU-only feature, with partial support on the X and none on the AIR or PRO.
availability_note: Unitree's shop sells the Go2 with an add-to-cart button and says orders ship within one month. The EDU version is bought by contacting Unitree's sales team.

hardware.compute: An 8-core high-performance CPU, which the product page says supports advanced, AI, and 3D-mapping modes. A high-computing-power module such as Orin is listed as an accessory.
hardware.sensors: Unitree's self-developed 4D LiDAR L2 with 360-by-96-degree hemispherical coverage and a 0.05 m minimum detection distance, an HD wide-angle camera, and a wireless vector positioning module on the PRO and above. The EDU version adds a foot-end force sensor.
hardware.actuation: Twelve joint motors with about 45 N·m peak joint torque. The product page lists payloads of about 7 to 8 kg, up to 10 to 12 kg maximum by configuration, and speeds up to 2.5 to 3.7 m/s, about 5 m/s maximum in lab tests.
hardware.power: An 8000 mAh smart battery with a 15000 mAh long-endurance option. The product page lists about 1 to 2 hours of battery life, about 2 to 4 on the EDU version, with a fast charger for the EDU.

developer_access: Unitree's unitree_rl_gym repository documents training a reinforcement-learning policy in simulation and deploying it to a physical Go2 for motion control, and its unitree_ros2 repository documents controlling the Go2 directly with ROS 2 messages, without wrapping the SDK interface. The product page gates full secondary development to the EDU version.
terms_note: Unitree's SDK, unitree_sdk2, is released under the BSD 3-Clause License. Unitree's terms page has Terms, After-sales Terms, Privacy Policy, Disclaimer, and End User License Agreement tabs; the after-sales tab is the hardware warranty policy. The product page lists a 6-month warranty for the AIR and 12 months for the other configurations.
not_verified: The documented policy interfaces are Unitree's own claims; the Atlas has not verified them. Every source is a Unitree web page or repository file that Unitree can change at any time.
